subject: EdgeOps regional processing split — new EU processor and evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@edgeops.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@edgeops.com, security@edgeops.com
Date: 2028-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Notice: regional processing split and EU subprocessor addition

Hi Rishi,

Hope you’re well — quick update from our infra team that impacts some customers in the EU. We are implementing a regional processing split for low-latency telemetry ingestion. As part of that effort we will onboard a small EU-based processor (DataWave GmbH) to handle ingestion within the EU region. The change is scoped to telemetry ingestion only (no model payload storage) and will apply to requests routed to EU endpoints after the cutover window on 2028-04-12.

Actionable items for Redwood:
- Confirm whether this constitutes a subprocessor addition under our existing DPA and whether you need the full attestation/evidence package.
- If you require, we can provide: subprocessor roster CSV (attached), an updated dataflow diagram specific to the EU split (attached), and a SOC 2 snapshot for DataWave (available on request).
- Planned cutover: 2028-04-12 02:00 UTC (maintenance window). No customer data will be exported outside the EU for EU-routed requests.

Attachments: edgeops_subprocessor_roster_v1.csv, edgeops_eu_dataflow_v1.pdf

If you want a short call this week to walk through the diagram I can set something up with our infra and security leads.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Partnerships & Integrations | EdgeOps
elena.torres@edgeops.com
+44 20 7946 0123

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2028-03-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Notice: regional processing split and EU subprocessor addition

Kimberly / Lauren — forwarding an incoming partner notice from EdgeOps. They plan to onboard DataWave GmbH for EU-only telemetry ingestion. I flagged the attachments but want legal + security input on whether we need a formal subprocessor addendum, SOC2 from DataWave (they offered snapshot), or any additional mitigations before the planned cutover on 2028-04-12.

Questions I have:
- Is telemetry ingestion (non-persistent, ephemeral KV) treated as "subprocessing" under our existing DPA language for partners?
- If yes, do we require documented encryption-at-rest proofs or only transit/TLS assurances for ephemeral ingestion?
- Any required customer notifications or procurement sign-offs?

Can you advise on the minimal evidence package to accept the change and any redlines we should push to EdgeOps? I can loop in account if necessary but prefer to resolve compliance items first.

Rishi
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: legal-team@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-29T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Notice: regional processing split and EU subprocessor addition

Thanks for the ping, Rishi. I reviewed the attachments and sketched an evidence checklist we should request before we mark this as non-material. High level notes below — I copied Legal to begin a quick review of the DPA language.

Immediate asks we should send to EdgeOps (minimal evidence):
1) DataWave GmbH SOC 2 snapshot or equivalent security assessment (latest 12 months).
2) Signed subprocessor clause acknowledgement from EdgeOps confirming DataWave will only process EU-routed telemetry and will not export those payloads outside the EU.
3) Updated dataflow diagram showing where keys are held and whether ingestion data is persisted and for how long (the diagram they sent is high level — ask for TTL and retention for EU ingestion).
4) Confirmation of encryption in transit (TLS1.3) and whether any at-rest encryption keys for EU ingestion are customer-specific or shared.
5) A short runbook describing incident escalation — who will notify Redwood if DataWave has a breach affecting EU telemetry.

Legal redline (quick): if EdgeOps adds DataWave and it processes any customer identifiers, we should require a Data Processing Addendum addendum (simple subprocessor schedule) and an option to require onshore fallback for specific regulated customers. Asking Legal to confirm the precise DPA trigger language but I believe the current DPA requires prior notice and the option to object for material changes.

Lauren — can you check whether any active Redwood customers routed to EU have contractual residency restrictions that would require an explicit objection/approval? If yes we need to surface that to EdgeOps and potentially delay cutover.

I suggest we ask for the minimal evidence above by EOD Fri 2028-04-01 to keep their timeline. If they can't provide the SOC2 snapshot we can ask for compensating controls (e.g., ISO27001 cert + right-to-audit clause).

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@edgeops.com>

Cc: compliance@edgeops.com, security@edgeops.com
Date: 2028-03-29T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: regional processing split and EU subprocessor addition

Hi Kimberly, Rishi — thanks for the quick review and the checklist. We can provide everything you requested. Attaching: edgeops_subprocessor_roster_v1.csv (contains DataWave entry), edgeops_eu_dataflow_v1.pdf (expanded), and edgeops-soc2-snapshot-2027.pdf (DataWave SOC2 redacted summary).

Quick answers to your questions:
- Retention: EU ingestion is ephemeral — TTL is 7 days by default; we can reduce to 3 days on request for customers with residency constraints. No model payloads are persisted.
- Encryption: TLS1.3 in transit; at-rest for EU ingestion is AES-256 with keys stored in a regional KMS. Keys are not shared with non-EU regions.
- Incident runbook: attached in the dataflow PDF appendix — EdgeOps will notify Redwood within 48 hours of any confirmed incident affecting telemetry.
- Contract: EdgeOps confirms subprocessor clause acknowledgement; compliance can send a short signed schedule if Redwood needs a formal addendum.

We are open to a 30-minute sync with infra + security to walk through the diagram before the cutover. If you want us to delay the cutover for specific customers we can hold the migration per-customer.

Best,
Elena
Partnerships & Integrations | EdgeOps
Attachments: edgeops_subprocessor_roster_v1.csv; edgeops_eu_dataflow_v1.pdf; edgeops-soc2-snapshot-2027.pdf
